Sam Turner: kicking off a small probe to refine continuous-batcher classification. want to try a two-axis hashmap: prompt_length_bucket x decode_rate_bucket to pick kernel and token-budget targets.
Mae Chen: nice. what's your initial bucket boundaries?
Sam Turner: thinking coarse to start: length buckets = [0-64,65-256,257-1024,1025+], decode rate = slow/med/fast (measured tokens/sec on decode sampling).  target token budget per batch by bucket.
Igor Petrov: curious how you plan to measure decode rate up-front. online estimation? histogram over last N requests?
Sam Turner: online EWMA per client + short-term probe samples from the admission queue. keep probe weight low so we don't perturb latency.
Lina Gomez: agree on EWMA. also we should tie kernel selection to median decode rate per bucket, not mean — heavy tails screw median kernel choice.
Sam Turner: yes. plan: maintain both median and 90p. median -> primary kernel, 90p -> fallback kernel for fast bursts.
perf-bot: regression alert suppressed: 2.3% p50 increase on last canary when token budget was bumped globally.
Igor Petrov: that alert matches my run. global bump raised batch sizes on short decodes and killed small-kernel throughput. we need bucket-level token budgets.
Mae Chen: proposed initial token_budget table (samples):
```
length_bucket  decode_rate  token_budget_target
0-64          fast         48
0-64          med          32
0-64          slow         16
65-256        fast         128
65-256        med          96
65-256        slow         64
257-1024      fast         256
257-1024      med          192
257-1024      slow         128
1025+         any          64  # cap to avoid huge batch mem usage
```
Lina Gomez: those look sensible. for 1025+, cap is smart. maybe 64 is low for long prompts; but kernel benefits diminish, and KV memory hits are huge.
Sam Turner: kernel mapping idea: prefer small-kernel (tight mem, lower throughput) for slow decode rate and tiny prompts; prefer large-kernel optimized for parallel decode on fast-rate buckets.
Igor Petrov: we should add a quick profile to map kernel choice to p95 tail under mixed coalescing. i'm worried about jitter when admission mixes rates.
Sam Turner: agreed. plan to run two probes this week: 1) offline trace-replay to measure kernel handoffs, 2) live canary on 5% traffic with bucketed budgets and EMAs.
perf-bot: note: enable KV-prefetch logging for live canary to measure cache hit-rate by bucket.
Mae Chen: small ask: add histogram for prefix-KV reuse length; many long prompts reuse a lot and could benefit from prefix caching instead of batch expansion.
Sam Turner: will add. also adding a short CL to admission that forces one probe per N requests to get stable decode-rate estimates.
Lina Gomez: one more: implement soft fallback policy — if chosen kernel's p95>target, immediately route that bucket to fallback kernel for next M minutes. prevents prolonged regressions. :thumbsup:
Sam Turner: good. risk checklist: stats noise, extra logging cost, and complexity in rollout. will draft rollout playbook.
Igor Petrov: during replay, measure these signals: batch_size distribution, token_budget_used, decode_rate_variance, kv_hit_rate, kernel_switch_count. export as traces.
Sam Turner: noted. will post probe configs and replay script later. anyone object to proceeding?
Mae Chen: go for it.
Lina Gomez: go for it.
deploy-bot: canary deployment scheduled: 2027-11-15T04:30Z -> targeting 5% traffic for lengthrate-hashmap-batcher
Sam Turner: thanks all — will update thread with results and short summary table once probes complete.
